thread:
leo.finance: FYI — EtherHealth wire hit our payment gateway flagged for mismatch. Their invoice INV-4821 shows reserved commit lines but our system recorded 0 committed hours for March. They’re asking for immediate correction before month-end closing. :eyes:
sara.ops: Can you drop the invoice PDF and the metering dump? I want to see the attribution between reserved vs burst.
billing-bot: Invoice INV-4821 uploaded: https://invoices.redwood/INV-4821.pdf
billing-bot: Metering snapshot (summary): committed_hours=0, burst_tokens=1,234,567, reserved_bucket=50%
kyle.sales: This is from an onboarding bundle — we promised an uplifted commit in contract addendum. Did that commit actually get provisioned?
leo.finance: Contract addendum S-2024-97 shows reserved commit=3x GPU-months, effective 2026-02-01. Ops deployed a capacity tag but it looks like the account never linked to the reserved pool.
sara.ops: Can ops confirm tagging? If not, two options: 1) reissue invoice with burst only, or 2) apply a one-time corrective allocation and issue a positive invoice adjustment + SLA credit.
natalie.revenue: We need finance approval for any goodwill credit. How big is the exposure if we apply corrective allocation retroactively?
leo.finance: Quick calc — if we apply retro reserve and backfill, estimated revenue recognized change = $18,250, but customer has already paid $14,000 in bursts; net due to customer would be ~$4,250 credit. If we do goodwill SLA credit instead, recommended cap = $6,000 to keep margin buffer.
kyle.sales: EtherHealth is a high-touch midmarket; Sales prefers goodwill credit to avoid churn unless legal needs a corrected invoice for audit.
sara.ops: Legal and contracts on call? If we reissue invoice, needs contract sign-off.
natalie.revenue: Approve up to $6,000 goodwill SLA-style credit contingent on ops confirming tag failure and a blameless postmortem. Please add ledger notes.
leo.finance: Confirming: request formal approval from @natalie.revenue — please reply with "approve" or "decline". Also need ops to run this query and paste output:
```
SELECT customer_id, sum(burst_tokens) as burst, sum(committed_hours) as committed
FROM metering.events
WHERE customer_id = 'cust_etherhealth' AND month = '2026-03'
GROUP BY customer_id;
```
sara.ops: Ran the query, output: burst=1,234,567, committed=0. Tagging shows 'reserved_pool:missing' on their account. Screenshot uploaded.
leo.finance: OK marking for credit. @kyle.sales please confirm customer communication template (we'll call it a "goodwill operational credit") so CS can send.
kyle.sales: Drafted message, short + transparent: "We found a provisioning mismatch that caused your reserved commit not to apply; we've issued a one-time operational credit of $6,000 while we fix the config." Posting to CS thread for review. :+1:
sara.ops: Ops will fix the tag, add guard to automations to alert on 'reserved_pool:missing' going forward. Will create a runbook entry.
leo.finance: Action items summarized: (1) apply $6,000 credit to customer account (finance action), (2) ops fix tag and run verification (ops), (3) sales/CS send customer note (sales), (4) postmortem and runbook (ops).
natalie.revenue: approve
leo.finance: Approved. I'll create the adjustment, reference INV-4821 and ledger entry ADJ-2026-177. Noting SLA-credit category = operational_goodwill, amount=6000.
billing-bot: Ledger entry created: ADJ-2026-177 | customer: cust_etherhealth | amount: -6000 | reason: operational goodwill credit | linked_invoice: INV-4821
sara.ops: Thx everyone. I'll follow up with the postmortem and tag fix timestamp. :white_check_mark:
